text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prosecutors warn against forming a police state in a written statement highlighting the misdeeds of the police force in dealing with people in custody.

- The Islamist Welfare Party is gearing up to change three articles of the constitution, two concerning the military and one on the lifting of prison terms for fathers who marry off their daughters in Moslem ceremonies before they are 15.
- Turkish hospitals are in a pitiful state. Emergency services are ill-equipped and understaffed and some patients have to be left to die.
- The strictly secular armed forces react strongly to the Islamist prime minister's attempts at rapprochement with Iran.
- Prosecutor quits case in disgust after the rejection of his demands parliamentary immunity be stripped from a former interior minister who resigned over a security scandal.
- The Kerkuk-Yumurtalik oil pipeline, which pumps oil from Iraq to Turkey, reopened after a six-year break.
- Markets are shocked by the S&P downgrading of Turkey's credit rating.
- A Turkish intellegence service report on gangs is expected to be finished by the weekend. The report hints at ties between top government figures and organised crime.
- A U.S-led allied air force based in Turkey to protect Iraqi Kurds will undergo cosmetic changes.
